name: Boot_Reset
purpose: reset vector: on a cold start (ports $A10008/$A1000C read 0) runs the standard Sega init (TMSS 'SEGA' write, 24 VDP registers, VRAM fill, Z80 stub, 64 KB RAM clear, CRAM/VSRAM clear, PSG mute), then falls into the region check

name: Boot_CheckRegion
purpose: compares the console's region (version register $A10001 bits 7-6 mapped through Tbl_RegionByVersion) with the header region string Hdr_Regions; a match continues the boot, anything else draws the 'DEVELOPED FOR USE ONLY WITH ... SYSTEMS.' lockout screen and hangs

name: Boot_DrawLockoutText
purpose: writes one 0-terminated lockout-screen string to the plane at VRAM $C000 (64 cells wide) at row d1, column d0, one tile per character (tile = char - $20)

name: Boot_InitIOPorts
purpose: after the region check passes: waits for any VDP DMA to finish, clears the three serial-control registers, sets the pad/expansion port control registers to $40 (TH as output) and jumps into the game's main init at $9E02

name: VM2_RunObject
purpose: object handler that runs one frame of an object's a2 script: saves sp in g_VM2SavedSP, loads a3/a4/a5 from the object's block handles $8/$A/$C(a6) and resumes the script at $2A(a4); a yield op restores sp and returns

name: Op2_SkipWord
purpose: a2 op / shared tail: skips one script word (a branch offset that is not taken) and continues (NEXT)

name: Op2_Native
purpose: a2 op: leaves the script and runs the 68000 code that follows it (jmp (a2)); that code returns to script with `jsr VM2_Enter`, which resumes right after the jsr

name: Obj_Destroy
purpose: tears down the current script object: notifies its spawn group (SpawnAction_GroupMemberGone with $1A(a6)) when its spawn action $19(a6) is 1, subtracts its population weight $18(a6) from g_ObjPopulation, releases its sprite frames and collision boxes, then unlinks it from its object list (when +4 prev is set) and returns its pool blocks

name: Obj_ReleaseFrames
purpose: releases every sprite frame an object holds: calls Spr_ReleaseFrame for each of the $14(a5) frame words at the start of the sprite block a5, clearing each, then zeroes the count

name: Op2_RunSpawnAction
purpose: a2 op: when the object has a spawn action ($19(a6) nonzero), clears it and runs entry $19 of Tbl_012EF0 (SpawnAction_Run) at the object's position with d1 = its argument $1A(a6); continues (NEXT)

name: Op2_LoadPalette1
purpose: a2 op: copies the 16-colour palette at the long operand into palette buffer line 1 ($E0F2, Pal_LoadLine1, which also flags it for upload); continues

name: Op2_SetAnim
purpose: a2 op: starts a sprite animation: stores the relative-word target as the animation script pointer $2E(a5), resets its timer $1E(a5) and clears the done flag (bit 0 of $18(a5)); continues

name: Op2_SetTimer0RandYield0
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 0: sets timer 0 ($1A(a4)) to base + random(range) (Rand_Below), saves the next op in slot 0 ($38(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer2RandYield0
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 0: sets timer 2 ($1E(a4)) to base + random(range) (Rand_Below), saves the next op in slot 0 ($38(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer0Yield1
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 1: sets timer 0 ($1A(a4)) to the word operand, saves the next op in slot 1 ($3C(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer0Yield2
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 2: sets timer 0 ($1A(a4)) to the word operand, saves the next op in slot 2 ($40(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer2Yield2
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 2: sets timer 2 ($1E(a4)) to the word operand, saves the next op in slot 2 ($40(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer3Yield3
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 3: sets timer 3 ($20(a4)) to the word operand, saves the next op in slot 3 ($44(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_SetTimer3RandYield3
purpose: a2 op for coroutine 3: sets timer 3 ($20(a4)) to base + random(range) (Rand_Below), saves the next op in slot 3 ($44(a4)) and returns to the code that stepped the coroutine

name: Op2_LoopTimer0
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 0 ($1A(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches (back) while it is still running; at expiry clears it and continues; a timer already at 0 falls through

name: Op2_SetTimer1
purpose: a2 op: sets timer 1 ($1C(a4)) from a word operand

name: Op2_SetTimer1Rand
purpose: a2 op: sets timer 1 ($1C(a4)) to a random value below a range plus a base

name: Op2_TickTimer1Branch
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 1 ($1C(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches when it expires this run; a timer already at 0 skips the offset

name: Op2_LoopTimer1
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 1 ($1C(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches (back) while it is still running; at expiry clears it and continues; a timer already at 0 branches (zero test first)

name: Op2_SetTimer2
purpose: a2 op: sets timer 2 ($1E(a4)) from a word operand

name: Op2_LoopTimer2
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 2 ($1E(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches (back) while it is still running; at expiry clears it and continues; a timer already at 0 falls through

name: Op2_SetTimer3
purpose: a2 op: sets timer 3 ($20(a4)) from a word operand

name: Op2_TickTimer3Branch
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 3 ($20(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches when it expires this run; a timer already at 0 also branches (no zero test)

name: Op2_LoopTimer3
purpose: a2 op: counts timer 3 ($20(a4)) down by $30(a4) and branches (back) while it is still running; at expiry clears it and continues; a timer already at 0 branches (zero test first)

name: Op2_AllocSubBlock
purpose: a2 op: makes sure the object owns a pool block at the handle word a6+offset (allocates one with ObjPool_Alloc when it is 0) and clears the block's first 64 bytes; with the pool empty it backs a2 up to this op and yields, retrying next frame

name: Op2_ClearNewBlock
purpose: shared tail of Op2_AllocSubBlock: clears 64 bytes (16 longs) at a0 and continues the script; not dispatched as an op on its own

name: Op2_SavePos
purpose: a2 op: saves the object's position (x $3E, y $42, 16.16 longs) in $46/$4A(a6)

name: Op2_SetCurHeadingArg0
purpose: a2 op: sets the integer part of the current heading $C(a3) to g_VM2Arg0 & $3FF

name: Op2_AimAtArgPoint
purpose: a2 op: makes (g_VM2Arg0, g_VM2Arg1) the motion target (Mot_SetTarget) and points the target heading $A(a3) at it (atan2, Mot_Atan2)

name: Mot_SetTarget
purpose: stores a target point in the motion block ($14/$16(a3)) and classifies the direction to it: bit 3 of (a3) set when |dy| >= |dx| (vertical-dominant), bit 4 set when the dominant component is negative

name: Op2_BranchPastTarget
purpose: a2 op: branches when the object has reached or passed its motion target along the dominant axis in its direction of travel (bits 3/4 of (a3) from Mot_SetTarget), re-deriving the heading from the velocity as it does

name: Op2_LaunchAlongHeading
purpose: a2 op: sets the velocity to the cruise speeds $30/$34(a3) along the target heading $A(a3) ($18 = speed x * cos, $1C = speed y * sin, Tbl_059B22) and copies the cruise speeds into the target speeds $24/$2C

name: Mot_TurnTowardHeading
purpose: turns the current heading $C(a3) (16.16, 1024 per turn) toward the target heading $A(a3) by the turn rate $10(a3), the shorter way round, landing on the target instead of overshooting it

name: Op2_AddTargetY
purpose: a2 op: moves the motion target point's y $16(a3) by a signed word

name: Op2_TargetRandomScreen
purpose: a2 op: picks a random motion target near the screen centre: x = 160 + random within +-75, y = 112 + random within +-55 (screen pixels)

name: Op2_CruiseNow
purpose: a2 op: sets both velocities and both target speeds to the cruise speeds at once ($18/$1C and $24/$2C of a3 = $30/$34)

name: Op2_StopCruiseX
purpose: a2 op: clears the x cruise speed $30(a3), then the x target speed (falls into Op2_ClearTargetSpeedX)

name: Op2_BrakeXGotoIfStopped
purpose: a2 op: sets the x target speed $24(a3) to 0, then branches to its word operand if the x velocity $18(a3) is already 0, else skips the operand and continues

name: Op2_StopX
purpose: a2 op: stops horizontal motion at once: x target speed $24 and x velocity $18 of a3 set to 0

name: Mot_SeekScreenX
purpose: op tail of Op2_SeekScreenX/X4: compares the object's screen x (x $3E(a6) - g_CameraX) with the target x $14(a3): more than d1 left of it -> Op2_CruiseRight, d1 or more right of it -> Op2_CruiseLeft, else the x target speed is cleared

name: Mot_SeekScreenXOrBranch
purpose: op tail of Op2_SeekScreenX(8)OrBranch: screen x vs target x $14(a3) with tolerance d1; outside it skips the offset word and cruises right/left, inside it clears the x target speed and takes the branch

name: Op2_SeekWorldX8OrBranch
purpose: a2 op: Mot_SeekWorldXOrBranch with an 8-pixel tolerance

name: Mot_SeekWorldXOrBranch
purpose: op tail: like Mot_SeekScreenXOrBranch but compares the world x $3E(a6) with the target x $14(a3) (no camera offset)

name: Op2_SeekScreenY4
purpose: a2 op: Mot_SeekScreenY with a 4-pixel tolerance

name: Mot_SeekScreenY
purpose: op tail of Op2_SeekScreenY4: compares the screen y (y $42(a6) - g_CameraY) with the target y $16(a3): above it by more than d1 -> Op2_CruiseDown, d1 or more below -> Op2_CruiseUp, else the y target speed is cleared

name: Mot_SeekScreenYOrBranch
purpose: op tail of Op2_SeekScreenY(8)OrBranch: screen y vs target y $16(a3) with tolerance d1; outside it skips the offset and cruises down/up, inside it clears the y target speed and takes the branch

name: Op2_SeekWorldY8OrBranch
purpose: a2 op: Mot_SeekWorldYOrBranch with an 8-pixel tolerance

name: Mot_SeekWorldYOrBranch
purpose: op tail: like Mot_SeekScreenYOrBranch but compares the world y $42(a6) with the target y $16(a3)

name: Mot_AccelForDistance
purpose: computes the acceleration for a script move: distance word * speed factor S ($2E(a4)) / (T * (T + S/16) / 2) * tick^2 ($32(a4)), the arithmetic-series form of covering the distance in T timer units

name: Op2_ClearVelY
purpose: a2 op: sets the y velocity $1C(a3) to 0

name: Op2_CruiseDown
purpose: a2 op: sets the y target speed $2C(a3) to +|y cruise speed $34(a3)| (accelerate downward); also the 'target is below' exit of the Y seek ops

name: Op2_ClearTargetSpeedY
purpose: a2 op: sets the y target speed $2C(a3) to 0, so the steering tail brakes the y velocity by the y acceleration

name: Mot_JumpGravity
purpose: reads a height word and returns the gravity of a jump that rises that many pixels in the time word that follows (Mot_JumpGravityD1)

name: Mot_JumpGravityD1
purpose: computes the gravity g for a jump of height h in time T: with tick t = S/16 ($2E(a4)/16), g = 2h * 65536 * t^2 / (T * (T + t)), so decelerating from g*T/t to 0 over T/t runs covers h pixels

name: Mot_JumpLaunchSpeed
purpose: returns the launch speed of a jump: -(gravity d1) * runs to the peak, the runs being the time word just read (-2(a2)) / the tick

name: Op2_SetTerrainBoxB
purpose: a2 op: sets and enables terrain box B (bit 2 of (a3), collided first by the move op): offset $48/$4A, wall and floor masks $4C/$4E, contact results cleared

name: Op2_BranchWallMask
purpose: a2 op: branches when the last wall contact result $52(a3) shares a bit with the mask word

name: Op2_BranchFloorMask
purpose: a2 op: branches when the last floor contact result $54(a3) shares a bit with the mask word (landed on that kind of floor)

name: Op2_BranchNoWall
purpose: a2 op: branches when the last move hit no wall ($52(a3) = 0)

name: Op2_BranchNotFloorMask
purpose: a2 op: branches when the last floor result $54(a3) has none of the mask's bits

name: Op2_BranchTerrainCode
purpose: a2 op: branches when the byte $50(a3) (high byte of the terrain routine's d3, stored by the move op) equals the operand's low byte

name: Op2_IncVar0
purpose: a2 op: adds 1 to script variable 0 ($22(a4))

name: Op2_DecVar0Loop
purpose: a2 op: loop counter: decrements script variable 0 ($22(a4)) and branches while it is not zero

name: Op2_SwitchVar0Bits
purpose: a2 op: bit switch on script variable 0 ($22(a4)): walks n (offset, mask) word pairs and branches by the offset of the first pair whose mask shares a bit with the variable; no match continues after the table

name: Op2_DecVar1Loop
purpose: a2 op: loop counter on script variable 1: decrements $24(a4) and branches while it is not zero

name: Op2_BranchVar1Ne
purpose: a2 op: branches when script variable 1 ($24(a4)) differs from a word

name: Op2_BranchVar1Gt
purpose: a2 op: branches when script variable 1 ($24(a4)) is greater than a word (signed)

name: Op2_BranchVar1Lt
purpose: a2 op: branches when script variable 1 ($24(a4)) is less than a word (signed)

name: Op2_SetVar2
purpose: a2 op: sets script variable 2 (word $26(a4)) to a word

name: Op2_BranchVar2Any
purpose: a2 op: branches when script variable 2 ($26(a4)) has any of the mask's bits

name: Op2_SwitchVar2Bits
purpose: a2 op: the bit switch of Op2_SwitchVar0Bits on script variable 2 ($26(a4))

name: Op2_SetVar3
purpose: a2 op: sets script variable 3 (word $28(a4)) to a word

name: Op2_StopCoroutine0
purpose: a2 op: stops coroutine slot 0 by pointing $38(a4) back at Scr2_002D28 (a script that just returns), the slot's idle value from Obj_InitSpawned

name: Op2_StartCoroutine0Here
purpose: a2 op: points coroutine slot 0 ($38(a4)) at the next op and continues there, so the ops that follow run now and again on every Op2_StepCoroutine0 (a restart point for a coroutine body that ends in the return op)

name: Op2_StepCoroutine0
purpose: a2 op: runs coroutine slot 0 for one step: pushes the current a2 and continues at the slot's script; the coroutine comes back with the return op $2D2A (or a SetTimer..Yield0 op that saves its position first)

name: Op2_StartCoroutine1Here
purpose: a2 op: points coroutine slot 1 ($3C(a4)) at the next op and continues there (restart point for the following coroutine body)

name: Op2_StepCoroutine1
purpose: a2 op: runs coroutine slot 1 ($3C(a4)) for one step (pushes a2, continues at the slot; back through the return op $2D2A)

name: Op2_StartCoroutine2Here
purpose: a2 op: points slot 2 ($40(a4)) at the next op and continues there

name: Op2_CallSlot2Native
purpose: a2 op: calls slot 2 ($40(a4)) as a native 68000 routine (jsr), then continues the script

name: Op2_StartCoroutine3Here
purpose: a2 op: points coroutine slot 3 ($44(a4)) at the next op and continues there

name: Op2_StepCoroutine3
purpose: a2 op: runs coroutine slot 3 ($44(a4)) for one step (pushes a2, continues at the slot)

name: Op2_SpawnChild
purpose: a2 op: spawns a child object once: when the a6 field named by the operand is 0, calls the spawner with d4/d5 = own x/y and stores the new object's a6 there; a field already set, or a failed spawn, just continues

name: Op2_SpawnChildOrWait
purpose: a2 op: as Op2_SpawnChild, but when the spawn fails (pool full) it rewinds to itself and yields, retrying next frame

name: Obj_SyncChild
purpose: copies parent fields to the child in an a6 field by flag bits 15-8: x/y $3E/$42 -> $3E/$42, drawn pos $4E/$50 -> $4E/$50, x/y -> drawn pos, drawn pos -> x/y, add word pair to child x/y, add word pair to child drawn pos, sprite attr $38(a5) and depth $3A(a5) to the child's a5

name: Child_GetA4
purpose: helper for the child-object ops: reads a word a6 field offset and returns the child's a4 block; with no child it drops its caller's return address and continues the script (the op does nothing)

name: Child_A4OfHandle
purpose: shared tail of the Child_GetA4 helpers: turns the child a6 in d1 into its a4 block ($A of the child) and returns to the op

name: Op2_StartChildCoroutine0Rel
purpose: a2 op: starts the child object's coroutine slot 0 ($38 of its a4) at a relative script address in the parent's script; does nothing without a child

name: Op2_StopChildCoroutine1
purpose: a2 op: stops the child object's coroutine slot 1 (sets its $3C(a4) to Scr2_002D28)

name: Op2_StartChildCoroutine1Rel
purpose: a2 op: starts the child object's coroutine slot 1 ($3C of its a4) at a relative address in the parent's script

name: Op2_StartChildCoroutine2Rel
purpose: a2 op: starts the child object's coroutine slot 2 ($40 of its a4) at a relative address in the parent's script

name: Op2_StartChildCoroutine3Rel
purpose: a2 op: starts the child object's coroutine slot 3 ($44 of its a4) at a relative address in the parent's script

name: Op2_SetCounter0
purpose: a2 op: sets loop counter 0 ($14(a4)), counted per run by Op2_LoopCounter0 (not by the tick like the timers)

name: Op2_LoopCounter1
purpose: a2 op: decrements loop counter 1 ($16(a4)) and branches while it is above 0

name: Op2_LoopCounter2
purpose: a2 op: decrements loop counter 2 ($18(a4)) and branches while it is above 0

name: Op2_GosubAbsArgs
purpose: a2 op: calls an absolute script subroutine with four word arguments: stores them in the argument registers g_VM2Arg3, Arg2, Arg1, Arg0 (high words), pushes the return point and jumps

name: Op2_Return
purpose: a2 op: returns from a script subroutine or a coroutine step: pops a2 pushed by Op2_Gosub* or Op2_StepCoroutineN and continues there

name: Op2_CruiseToPlayerX
purpose: a2 op: cruises toward the targeted player's x without changing the facing (x target speed +cruise, or Op2_CruiseLeft); no target brakes x

name: Op2_SetRandJitter
purpose: a2 op: sets the object's random offset $1C(a6) to a value in [-w, w) (Rand_Next * w * 2 >> 16), so enemies sharing a script keep slightly different distances

name: Op2_HoldRangeOfPlayerX
purpose: a2 op: walks to stay a horizontal distance [near, far] (+ jitter $1C(a6)) from the targeted player on the side the object is on, in screen space, facing the player once there; a window pushed past the screen edge ($136/$A) is clamped, and when the object is within margin of the player's far side it goes round to the other side; stopped objects widen the window by 6 (hysteresis)

name: Op2_FaceCruiseToPlayerXTurnBranch
purpose: a2 op: as Op2_FaceCruiseToPlayerX (face and cruise toward the targeted player's x) and branches when that turned the object around

name: Op2_BranchPlayerInBox
purpose: a2 op: branches when the targeted player's collision box (box id = record +$3E) overlaps a rectangle given relative to the object, mirrored by its H/V flip bits

name: Mot_StorePlayerWindow
purpose: packs a player-relative window into the motion block: halves of d0/d1 into the bytes of $14(a3), of d2/d3 into $16(a3) (Op2_HoldPlayerWindow doubles them back), then continues the script

name: Op2_BranchTouchBox
purpose: a2 op: branches when any box on a collision list overlaps a rectangle relative to the object (mirrored by its H/V flip bits), remembering that box in g_FoundBox; the kind word picks the list through a jump table (0/4 = g_PlayerBoxList, 8 = g_EnemyBoxList)

name: Op2_BranchTouchBox_KindC
purpose: Op2_BranchTouchBox's jump-table slot for kind $C: the enemy-list case (bra.w Op2_BranchTouchBox_Enemies)

name: Op2_BranchTouchBox_Players
purpose: Op2_BranchTouchBox's g_PlayerBoxList case (kinds 0 and 4): Hitbox_FindPlayerBox on the prepared rectangle; also holds the shared not-found ($3760) and found ($376E) exits

name: Obj_SetAttackBoxes
purpose: rebuilds the script object's attack-box set from d7 inline specs: reuses or allocates a pool block per box, stamps owner a6 (+$2E), owner id $58 (+$10), serial $56 (+4), kind and rectangle (+6..+$E), hit callback (+$30, default the rts $82C) and its argument words; frees the boxes beyond the new count

name: Obj_SetBodyBoxes
purpose: rebuilds the script object's body-box set (the boxes it can be struck through) from d7 inline specs, as Obj_SetAttackBoxes does, also clearing each box's damage taken (+$20); surplus boxes are unlinked from their list (when +2 is set) and freed

name: Op2_BranchBoxStruck
purpose: a2 op: branches when the object's body box number i was struck (Obj_TestBoxStruck)

name: Obj_TestStruck
purpose: tests and clears the struck bit (bit 0 of +$3C) of the object's body boxes, stopping at the first one set

name: Obj_TestBoxStruck
purpose: tests and clears the struck bit of one body box chosen by a word operand (an index out of range or an empty slot counts as not struck)

name: Op2_SwitchAttacker
purpose: a2 op: branches by who struck the object: compares the attacker id of g_StruckBox (+$1A) with a list of (id, offset) pairs and takes the first match

name: Op2_SetVector0HereGotoArg
purpose: a2 op: stores a word in g_VM2Arg0, then as Op2_SetVector0HereGoto points script vector 0 ($32(a6)) at the op after the offset word and jumps to the offset

name: Op2_SetVector1HereGoto
purpose: a2 op: points script vector 1 ($36(a6)) at the op right after its offset word and continues at the offset target

name: Op2_GotoVector2Plus
purpose: a2 op: continues the script at script vector 2 plus a word displacement (an entry inside the block the vector points to)

name: Op2_GosubVector2Plus
purpose: a2 op: calls vector 2 plus a word displacement as a subroutine, returning to the op after the displacement

name: Op2_SwitchAimDir
purpose: a2 op: branches through a table of word offsets indexed by the sprite's aim direction ($1A(a5) / 4)

name: Op2_BranchWeaponLvlMaxGE
purpose: a2 op: branches when g_WeaponLvlMax (the best weapon level among players in play) is at least the operand

name: Op2_BranchStatGE
purpose: shared tail of the player-stat branch ops: branches when d0 >= the word operand; not dispatched as an op on its own

name: Op2_RunAnim
purpose: a2 op: steps the current sprite block's animation script: counts the frame timer $1E(a5) down by the object's speed $2E(a4) and, when it runs out, runs the animation script at $2E(a5) (ops chained by NEXT until one returns with rts) and saves where it stopped

name: Op2_SwitchHeading
purpose: a2 op: branches by the current heading split into n equal sectors: index = ((heading $C(a3) + rotation) & $3FE) * n / 1024

name: Op2_AnimFrame
purpose: animation-script op: shows a frame: points the sprite's draw list $2A(a5) at the inline block after the offset word (sprite ops ended by Op2_DrawEnd), continues the animation at the offset next time and holds for the display time $1C(a5)

name: Op2_SetSprVar0
purpose: a2 op: sets sprite-block variable 0 ($22(a5)), one of three words ($22/$24/$26) that player natives step as animation phases

name: Op2_SetSprVar1
purpose: a2 op: sets sprite-block variable 1 ($24(a5))

name: Op2_SetSprVar2
purpose: a2 op: sets sprite-block variable 2 ($26(a5))

name: Op2_BranchNotSection
purpose: a2 op: branches unless the current game section g_SectionId equals the operand

name: Op2_SetBlinkTimer
purpose: a2 op: sets the sprite's blink timer (byte $16(a5)): while it runs Op2_Draw skips drawing on alternate frames (the player's spawn invulnerability uses the same byte)

name: Op2_PlaySound
purpose: a2 op: plays sound effect d0 = operand through the driver request Snd_PlaySfx (8-byte entries of Tbl_1E50D6 with a priority check)

name: Op2_WaitPopBelow
purpose: a2 op: waits (yielding, retried every frame) until g_ObjPopulation is below the operand, then continues

name: Op2_StartA6Script
purpose: a2 op: starts a loader script on the global a6 VM (decompress/DMA jobs such as op $7120): stores its address in $E036, sets the per-frame resume hook $E03A = $70A8 (run from Frame_End by $7086) and the busy flag $F4BA

name: Op2_DrawInScreenBox
purpose: a2 op: draws the sprite (as Op2_Draw) only while its screen position (x - g_CameraX, y - g_CameraY) lies in x [left, right] and y [top, bottom)

name: Op2_DrawSprFront
purpose: draw-list op: draws one frame at the object's position in front of every sorted sprite (Spr_AddFront, no depth)

name: Op2_DrawSprBack
purpose: draw-list op: draws one frame at the object's position behind every sorted sprite (Spr_AddBack)

name: Op2_DrawSprAtDrawnDepth
purpose: draw-list op: Op2_DrawSprAtDrawn with a depth offset

name: Op2_DrawSprAtDrawnBack
purpose: draw-list op: draws one frame at the drawn position $4E/$50(a6) behind every sorted sprite (Spr_AddBack)

name: Op2_StepVelocity
purpose: a2 op: steps the motion block's velocity for this frame and leaves the frame's move in d1/d2 for the next op: each axis moves toward its target speed by its acceleration (copied to $38/$3C), then the decaying impulses $2/$6 are added; while the stun count $1(a3) runs the velocity part is 0

name: Op2_ApplyMoveBranchAtY
purpose: a2 op: adds this frame's move d1/d2 to x/y; when y reaches a word limit (from either side) it is clamped there and the script branches

name: Op2_ApplyMoveLandAtY
purpose: a2 op: adds this frame's move d1/d2 to x/y and lands on a floor at a word y: there y is clamped, the motion block's on-ground word $54(a3) set and its y velocity $1C(a3) cleared; off it $54(a3) is cleared

name: Op2_MoveTerrain
purpose: a2 op: moves the object by d1/d2 through the scene terrain: without terrain boxes it just adds the move; box B (bit 2 of (a3)) is collided first (wall/floor results $52/$54, d3 -> $50); if B finds no floor and box A (bit 1) is on, box A is collided, clearing the x/y velocity on wall/floor contact

name: Hitbox_TestAttackBox
purpose: tests one attack box at the object's position: Hitbox_TestAttackBoxAt with d1/d2 = x/y $3E/$42(a6)

name: Hitbox_TestAttackBoxAt
purpose: tests one attack box at position d1/d2: mirrors its rectangle by the sprite's flip bits, then by its kind word looks for overlapping boxes on g_PlayerBoxList (0 = first, 4 = all) or g_EnemyBoxList (8 = first) and strikes them

name: Hitbox_KindAllEnemies
purpose: entry $C of Hitbox_TestAttackBoxAt's kind jump table: attack-box kind $C goes to Hitbox_HitAllEnemyBoxes

name: Hitbox_HitFirstPlayerBox
purpose: attack-box kind 0: strikes the first box on g_PlayerBoxList that overlaps the rectangle, if any

name: Hitbox_HitAllEnemyBoxes
purpose: attack-box kind $C: strikes every box on g_EnemyBoxList that overlaps the rectangle

name: Hitbox_Strike
purpose: one hit: tags the struck box with the attacker's owner id and runs the attack box's hit callback, then the struck box's callback

name: Op2_TestAttackBoxAtDrawn
purpose: a2 op: tests one attack box, chosen by index, at the object's drawn position $4E/$50(a6), unless the attack pause count $1(a4) is running

name: Hitbox_LinkByKind_AllPlayers
purpose: Hitbox_LinkByKind entry for kind 4: appends the box to g_PlayerBoxList ($8C3C), as kind 0

name: Hitbox_LinkByKind_Enemy
purpose: Hitbox_LinkByKind entry for kind 8: appends the box to g_EnemyBoxList ($8C54)

name: Hitbox_LinkByKind_AllEnemies
purpose: Hitbox_LinkByKind entry for kind $C: appends the box to g_EnemyBoxList ($8C54), as kind 8

name: Op2_PlaceBodyBoxes_Off
purpose: tail of Op2_PlaceBodyBoxes while the body-box off count (a4) runs: decrements it and unlinks every linked body box (the object cannot be hit)

name: Op2_ClearMotionBlock
purpose: a2 op: zeroes the 64-byte block whose address is at $8(a6) (the motion block a3 is reset to by Op2_ResetA3), then NEXT

name: Op2_StopOsc
purpose: a2 op: stops both axes of the oscillator block in an a6 field by zeroing their max speeds (+$C, +$20), so Op2_StepOsc brakes them to rest

name: Op2_StopOscY
purpose: a2 op: stops the y axis of the oscillator block in an a6 field (max speed +$20 = 0)

name: Op2_FxSpawnOffAbs
purpose: a2 op: as Op2_FxSpawnOff with an absolute (dc.l) a4 script address

name: Op2_FxHeadingHere
purpose: a2 op: sets the effect-spawn heading d3 to the object's current heading $C(a3) (high word)

name: Op2_FxHeading
purpose: a2 op: sets the effect-spawn heading d3 to a word (0-$3FF, $400 a turn) in the high word

name: Op2_FxMarkPlayerTarget
purpose: a2 op: stores the targeted player's x/y (record +$2E/+$32 of $10(a4)) in g_ArcTargetX/Y for the effect script spawned next; with no target skips the next 4 script bytes

name: VM4_RunObject
purpose: object handler of every a4-VM object (installed by the spawn ops through $8A08): a5 = a6 (no child yet) and resumes the object's a4 script at its saved pc $8(a6)

name: VM4_Next
purpose: a4-VM NEXT: fetches the next op word from a4 and jumps to that handler; also the entry for native code that has set a4 and a6 itself

name: Op4_SetResume
purpose: a4 op: sets the object's resume pc $8(a6) to the operand address + word offset and continues here

name: Op4_SetTimer
purpose: a4 op: sets the object's timer word $16(a6)

name: Op4_BranchScreenYOutside
purpose: a4 op: compares the drawn y d5 minus g_CameraY with [lo, hi] and continues past the operands when inside; outside it branches

name: Op4_KillOffScreen
purpose: a4 op: deletes the object when its drawn position d4/d5 is outside the on-screen window (x - g_OnScreenLeft >= $170 or y - g_OnScreenTop >= $110, unsigned); otherwise continues

name: VM4_ResumeA5
purpose: a4 VM: continues the a4 script of the object in a5 from its saved pc $8(a5); the return point of Op4_ReplaceSelf's re-init

name: Op4_Spawn
purpose: a4 op: spawns a child a4 object ($613A: pool block on the object list, handler VM4_RunObject, owner $10 and attr $22 inherited, radius/heading/x/y from d2-d5 plus an optional parameter table) and continues with a5 = the child

name: Op4_SetDamage
purpose: a4 op: sets the damage word $12(a6) that the object's hit natives deal (Shot_DamageTarget adds it to the struck box +$20 and subtracts it from its energy)

name: Op4_JitterSpawnHeading
purpose: a4 op: adds a random amount in [-w/2, w/2) heading units ($400 per turn) to the spawn heading register d3

name: Op4_OffsetSpawnXY
purpose: a4 op: adds signed pixel offsets to the integer words of the spawn position registers d4/d5 (16.16)

name: Op4_OffsetSpawnHeading
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed amount to the integer word of the spawn heading register d3 ($400 units per turn), e.g. to fan out a row of spawns

name: Op4_AddVelY
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed 8.8 word (px/frame) to the object's y velocity $42 (16.16)

name: Op4_SaveDrawPos
purpose: a4 op: computes the object's drawn point ((x, y) + radius * (cos, sin)(heading)) and stores its pixel words in $56/$58(a6)

name: Op4_AddY
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed pixel word to the integer part of the object's y $32 (16.16)

name: Op4_AddAccelY
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed 8.8 word to the object's y acceleration $52

name: Op4_ChildAddX
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed pixel word to the integer part of the last spawned child's x $2E(a5)

name: Op4_ChildAddXY
purpose: a4 op: adds signed pixel words to the integer parts of the child's x and y ($2E/$32 of a5)

name: Op4_ChildAddY
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed pixel word to the integer part of the child's y $32(a5)

name: Op4_ChildAddHeading
purpose: a4 op: adds a signed word to the integer part of the child's heading $2A(a5) ($400 per turn)

name: Op4_JitterX
purpose: a4 op: moves the object's x $2E by a random [-w/2, w/2) px (16.16)

name: Op4_JitterXY
purpose: a4 op: moves the object's x $2E and y $32 by random [-wx/2, wx/2) / [-wy/2, wy/2) px

name: Op4_JitterHeading
purpose: a4 op: turns the object's heading $2A by a random [-w/2, w/2) units ($400 per turn)

name: Op4_JitterVelX
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [-w/2, w/2) (8.8 px/frame) to the object's x velocity $3E

name: Op4_RangeVelX
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8 px/frame) to the object's x velocity $3E

name: Op4_ScatterVelY
purpose: a4 op: kicks the object's y velocity $42 by base + a random [0, w/2) (8.8) up or down at random

name: Op4_RandVelRadius
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [0, w) (8.8) to the object's radius velocity $36

name: Op4_JitterAccelX
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [-w/2, w/2) (8.8) to the object's x acceleration $4E

name: Op4_RangeAccelX
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8) to the object's x acceleration $4E

name: Op4_RangeAccelY
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8) to the object's y acceleration $52

name: Op4_RangeAccelRadius
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8) to the object's radius acceleration $46

name: Op4_ChildJitterX
purpose: a4 op: moves the last spawned child's x $2E(a5) by a random [-w/2, w/2) px

name: Op4_ChildJitterXY
purpose: a4 op: moves the child's x/y ($2E/$32 of a5) by random [-wx/2, wx/2) / [-wy/2, wy/2) px

name: Op4_ChildJitterHeading
purpose: a4 op: turns the child's heading $2A(a5) by a random [-w/2, w/2) units ($400 per turn)

name: Op4_ChildRangeVelX
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8 px/frame) to the child's x velocity $3E(a5)

name: Op4_ChildRandVelY
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [0, w) (8.8 px/frame; w may be negative) to the child's y velocity $42(a5)

name: Op4_ChildScatterVelRadius
purpose: a4 op: kicks the last spawned child's radius velocity $36(a5) by base + a random [0, w/2) (8.8), outward or inward at random

name: Op4_ChildJitterAccelX
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [-w/2, w/2) (8.8) to the last spawned child's x acceleration $4E(a5)

name: Op4_ChildRangeAccelX
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8) to the child's x acceleration $4E(a5)

name: Op4_ChildRandAccelY
purpose: a4 op: adds a random [0, w) (8.8; w may be negative) to the child's y acceleration $52(a5)

name: Op4_ChildRangeAccelY
purpose: a4 op: adds base + a random [0, w) (8.8) to the child's y acceleration $52(a5) (gravity spread for debris)

name: Op4_ForkOrBranch
purpose: a4 op: forks a child a4 object (VM4_Fork: script at operand + offset, motion from d2-d5) and continues; when the pool is full it branches instead

name: Op4_Fork
purpose: a4 op: forks a child a4 object (VM4_Fork) running the script at operand + offset; continues with the next op (child ops then edit a5); a full pool ends this run

name: Op4_ForkAndEnd
purpose: a4 op: forks a child a4 object running the script at operand + offset and ends this run (Op4_Fork's child, Op4_ForkAbsAndEnd's end)

name: Op4_ForkRestAndEnd
purpose: a4 op: forks a child whose script is the rest of this one (the ops after this word) and ends this run, so a parent that resumes here emits one child per frame

name: VM4_Fork
purpose: spawns a child a4 object with script a3: pool block on the object list (handler VM4_RunObject), owner $10 and attr $22 inherited, anim/frames/box/depth cleared, radius/heading/x/y = d2-d5, velocities and accelerations 0

name: VM4_SpawnChild
purpose: spawn core of Op4_Spawn*: allocates a child a4 object and sets its script and motion from d2-d5 plus an optional 48-byte parameter table; on a full pool drops the caller's return and ends the run or takes the failure branch

name: Op4_SpawnAtDrawPos
purpose: a4 op: sets the spawn position registers d4/d5 to the object's drawn point (16.16), so the next spawn starts where the object is drawn

name: VM4_CalcDrawPos
purpose: computes an a4 object's drawn point: d4/d5 = (x, y) + radius * (cos, sin)(heading), 16.16

name: Op4_SpawnHeadingFromSelf
purpose: a4 op: sets the spawn heading register d3 to the object's heading $2A and the spawn radius d2 to 0

name: Op4_BounceYRandom
purpose: a4 op: bounces the object: y velocity $42 = -(v/2 + a random [0, 1/4) of v/2's integer part), a reversed, roughly halved, slightly randomised rebound

name: Op4_BranchScriptTimerZero
purpose: a4 op: branches when the shared countdown g_ScriptTimer has run out (0); otherwise continues past the offset

name: Op4_AltTerrainMoveOrFall
purpose: a4 op: moves $56/$58 to d4/d5 against the alternative terrain g_TerrainFnAlt (masks 9/$B) and branches when there is no floor contact (falling); on a floor continues

name: Op4_BranchTouchPlayer
purpose: a4 op: branches when a player box overlaps the box d4 +- w by d5 +- h around the drawn point (Hitbox_FindPlayerBox); otherwise continues past the offset

name: Op4_TakeHitPhaseA
purpose: a4 op: gives the object the next frame phase $18 from the toggling g_FxPhaseA, so successive player shots run their hit tests on alternate frames

name: Op4_BodyBox
purpose: a4 op: keeps a shootable box on the object: creates it on first use (enemy box list, id, energy, no hit callback) and recentres it on d4/d5 every run; branches once the box's energy is used up

name: Op4_DrawKillSidesBelowOrClear
purpose: a4 op: deletes the object during a screen clear or when d4/d5 is off the sides or below the on-screen window (above the top is kept); otherwise draws it (Op4_Draw), ending the frame

name: Op4_SetShotFrames
purpose: a4 op (shots): sets the object's frame ring $C (cyclic list of {next-node long, sprite-data long}) and its resume pc $8 to the next op

name: VM5_Yield
purpose: a5-VM yield tail (not dispatched): ends this frame's run of the wave script: saves the pc in $1E(a6) and returns through the saved stack pointer (the timer set by the op before decides when it resumes)

name: Op5_Wait
purpose: a5 op: waits t/16 frames (timer $2E = t * 16, counted down only while the population is below the cap), then continues

name: Op5_SetLoopA0
purpose: a5 op: sets loop counter A $1A(a6) to 0 (an Op5_LoopA then falls through at once)

name: Op5_LoopA
purpose: a5 op: counts loop counter A $1A(a6) down and branches back while it stays above 0; at 0 continues past the offset

name: Op5_SetLoopB2
purpose: a5 op: sets loop counter B $1C(a6) to 2

name: Op5_SetLoopB5
purpose: a5 op: sets loop counter B $1C(a6) to 5 (the 4 and 6-8 entries around it never ran and stay raw)

name: Op5_SetLoopB
purpose: a5 op: sets loop counter B $1C(a6) to a word

name: Op5_LoopB
purpose: a5 op: counts loop counter B $1C(a6) down and branches back while it stays above 0; at 0 continues past the offset (the outer/inner twin of Op5_LoopA)

name: Op5_SetQuota
purpose: a5 op: sets the wave's spawn quota $E (one player) / $10 (two players) and the script address $16 it jumps to once that many enemies spawned; clears the spawn count $C

name: Op5_SetOrigin
purpose: a5 op: sets the wave's spawn origin offset $26/$28 (x, y words)

name: Op5_AddOriginX
purpose: a5 op: adds a signed word to the spawn origin x offset $26 (spawns marching along a row)

name: Op5_LockCameraHere
purpose: a5 op: locks the camera where it is: g_CameraLockX = g_CameraX + $A0 (16.16), so Camera_TrackPlayersX holds the view for an arena fight

name: Op5_ShowGoSign
purpose: a5 op: shows the GO! sign (HUD_ShowGoSignCb), which releases the camera lock when it arrives

name: Op5_WaitPopulation6
purpose: a5 op: waits until g_ObjPopulation is at most 6

name: VM5_CloseGroup
purpose: closes a wave's kill group at the wave's end: its member target becomes the spawned count, and the block is freed if all of those are already dead

name: SpawnAction_GroupMemberGone
purpose: spawn action 2, and Obj_Destroy's call for an object that still carries action 1 (removed, e.g. off screen, without its kill counted): counts the member as gone (+8) and frees the group block once that reaches the member target (+0); no reward

name: VM5_SpawnEntry
purpose: spawns one enemy from an a5 wave spawn entry: position from the entry (screen-relative or world) plus the wave origin, then the entry's spawner; on success counts the spawn and hands the new object its spawn action (action 1 also joins the wave's open kill group)

name: VM6_RunHook
purpose: runs the a6 loader script's per-frame resume hook: jumps to g_A6ResumeHook when it is set, otherwise returns

name: VM6_StartFromTrigger
purpose: stage trigger callback that starts the a6 loader script given by the trigger entry's argument long (loads the next section's graphics while the stage scrolls)

name: VM6_Start
purpose: starts an a6 loader script: stores its pc and sets the resume hook to VM6_Resume so Frame_End runs it from the next frame

name: VM6_Run
purpose: runs an a6 loader script right now from a scene setup: dispatches its first op; the script runs on until an op parks it for Frame_End (decompress in the background, V-int jobs, queued DMA) or ends

name: VM6_Resume
purpose: the a6 VM's resume hook: clears g_A6ResumeHook and continues the loader script at g_A6ScriptPc

name: Op6_CallNative
purpose: a6 op: calls a native routine (dc.l) with a6 at its inline arguments and continues after it

name: VM6_LoadPalettes
purpose: a6 helper: finds a palette entry in a scene buffer and copies count palettes from it into CRAM lines chosen 2 bits at a time by a mask byte (Pal_LoadLine0-3)

name: VM6_InitLayer
purpose: shared tail of the a6 layer-init ops: Layer_Init on layer a1 with the level header from a g_BufPtrs slot and the script's tile word, then continues

name: Op6_ClearPlane
purpose: a6 op: fills a whole VDP plane with the blank tile $5FC through a V-int job (a few rows per V-int), parking the script until it is done

name: VM6_SetupClearRect
purpose: a6 helper: sets up a plane fill job: fill tile $5FC, the VDP write command of the rectangle's first row and the column/row counts (0 = the whole plane width/height)

name: VM6_StartClearJob
purpose: a6: starts the plane-fill V-int job: allocates a V-int list object (retrying each frame while the pool is full) with handler VM6_VIntClearRows, and parks the script

name: Op6_MoveLayerAToCamera
purpose: a6 op: places map layer g_LayerA at the camera position plus an offset (Layer_MoveX/Layer_MoveY, no drawing) and continues

name: Op6_RedrawLayerA
purpose: a6 op: redraws a full screen of map layer g_LayerA one block column per frame through the tile queue, parking the script until done

name: VM6_StartRedraw
purpose: a6: starts a column-per-frame redraw of a layer: saves its block column +$26 and plane column +$32, takes the column count g_ScreenBlocksX from +$3E and installs VM6_RedrawStep

name: VM6_SetupMapBlit
purpose: a6 helper: sets up a cell-map blit from a buffer entry (word width, word height, then cell words): source row pointer and stride, tile word, the VDP write command of the destination and the column/row counts (clipped to the plane)

name: VInt_Handler
purpose: vertical-blank interrupt: flushes the DMA queue, runs V-int objects, reads pads, ticks sound and fades, parks the background task

name: DMA_ResetQueue
purpose: empties the VDP DMA queue and refills this frame's DMA budget

name: DMA_FlushQueue
purpose: writes every queued 14-byte DMA command (VDP regs $93-$97 + the two command words) to the VDP control port

name: DMA_FlushQueue_40
purpose: head of DMA_FlushQueue's unrolled copy: entered with no free slot, so all 40 queued DMA commands are sent (two 8-byte units here, the rest in DMA_FlushQueue_38 onward)

name: DMA_FlushQueue_38
purpose: computed entry into DMA_FlushQueue's unrolled copy that sends 38 queued DMA commands (2 slots free)

name: DMA_FlushQueue_29
purpose: computed entry into DMA_FlushQueue's unrolled copy that sends 29 queued DMA commands (11 slots free)

name: DMA_Reserve
purpose: reserves d0 DMA queue slots and d1 units of this frame's DMA budget, returning where to write the commands

name: Spr_QueueSATDMA
purpose: terminates the sprite link chain and queues the DMA of the sprite attribute buffer $FF9B56 to VRAM $0000

name: Spr_ResetList
purpose: clears the per-frame sprite display list: 80 free entries, empty depth-sorted list, empty front list, SAT buffer write pointer at its start

name: Spr_AddSorted
purpose: adds a sprite frame to the display list in descending order of d7 (earlier = higher SAT priority = drawn in front)

name: Spr_AddBack
purpose: appends a sprite frame after the last entry of the sorted display list, so it is drawn behind everything added so far

name: Spr_AddFront
purpose: appends a sprite frame to the unsorted front list, which Spr_BuildSAT emits before the sorted list (in front of all sorted sprites)

name: Spr_BuildSAT
purpose: walks the front list then the sorted display list and writes each frame's pieces into the sprite attribute buffer, clipped to the screen, at most 80 sprites

name: Spr_DrawDirect
purpose: draws one sprite frame straight into the SAT buffer, bypassing the display list, using the adjustable clip window

name: Spr_EmitClipped
purpose: emits the pieces of one frame into the SAT buffer, clipping against the window g_SprDirectMaxY/MaxX and biasing by g_SprDirectBiasY/BiasX

name: Spr_InitBankFrames
purpose: builds RAM frame-table entries for a loaded sprite bank, dropping any art still held by the bank's handles

name: Spr_ChangeFrame
purpose: switches a sprite from frame d2 to frame d1, loading the new frame's art into VRAM when it uses a different art handle

name: Spr_SwapFrameArt
purpose: acquires VRAM art for a sprite's new frame (allocating blocks and queuing its DMA when not resident) and releases the old frame's art

name: Spr_ReleaseFrame
purpose: drops one reference to the art of frame d2; at the last one its blocks count as free and its descriptor goes on the release ring for later eviction

name: Spr_QueueArtDMA
purpose: queues one DMA per art chunk from ROM into the frame's allocated 16-tile VRAM blocks and charges the DMA budget

name: ArtCache_Init
purpose: sets up the sprite-art VRAM cache: d1 16-tile blocks from tile $5F, 50 descriptors, empty release ring, all art handles cleared

name: ArtCache_AddBlocksInline
purpose: adds blocks to the sprite-art VRAM cache, the count read from the inline word at (a6)+

name: ArtCache_AddBlocks
purpose: appends d0 more 16-tile VRAM blocks, continuing from g_ArtNextBlockTile, to the free block ring

name: ArtCache_Alloc
purpose: gives an art handle a descriptor and d1 VRAM blocks, evicting released art from the release ring when the free ring runs short

name: ArtCache_Release
purpose: drops one reference to the art behind handle a0; at the last one the blocks count as free and the descriptor is queued on the release ring

name: ObjPool_Init
purpose: links d0 blocks of $5A bytes at a0 into the object pool's free list

name: ObjPool_Alloc
purpose: pops one $5A-byte block off the object pool's free list without clearing it

name: ObjPool_AllocClear
purpose: pops one block off the object pool and zeroes all $5A bytes of it

name: ObjPool_Free
purpose: pushes the $5A-byte block a0 back onto the object pool's free list

name: Obj_RunList
purpose: calls the per-frame handler of every object on the main object list $DE8C, with a6 = the object

name: Obj_ListEnd
purpose: handler of the main object list's tail sentinel: drops the jsr return address so Obj_RunList itself returns

name: Obj_InitList
purpose: empties the main object list: links the head node g_ObjListHead straight to the tail sentinel g_ObjListTail and gives the sentinel the handler Obj_ListEnd

name: Obj_LinkAtEnd
purpose: appends an already-built object a0 to the end of the main object list (just before g_ObjListTail), so Obj_RunList runs it from the next walk

name: Obj_NewMultiFail
purpose: failure exit of Obj_NewMulti / Obj_NewMultiUnlinked when the pool holds fewer than d7 blocks: gives the d7 back to g_ObjPoolFree and returns -1

name: Obj_NewMulti
purpose: creates a d7-block object: pops d7 pool blocks, makes the first the object (handler a0, linked at the end of the main list), stores the other d7-1 block addresses as handles from +8 and zeroes the rest of the 8 handle words up to +$17

name: Obj_NewMulti_HandleRun
purpose: unrolled run of 4-byte units (move.w a2,(a1)+ / movea.w (a2),a2) that writes the next pool block's address into the object's next handle word and walks the free list; this label is the 8-block entry

name: Obj_NewMulti_ClearRun
purpose: unrolled move.w d0,(a1)+ run that zeroes the handle words Obj_NewMulti_HandleRun left over (9 - blocks of them, so +8..+$17 are always written)

name: Obj_NewMulti_Clear4
purpose: the clear-run entry used by 4-block objects (5 handle words left to zero), then the end of Obj_NewMulti: stores a2 as the new pool head and returns success

name: Obj_NewMultiAfter
purpose: Obj_NewMulti linked right after the running object a6 instead of before the main list's tail: pops d7 pool blocks, makes the first the object (handler a0) and shares Obj_NewMulti's handle and clear runs

name: Obj_NewClear
purpose: creates a one-block object on the main list: pops a pool block, sets its handler a0, links it before g_ObjListTail and zeroes +8..+$17

name: Obj_New
purpose: creates a one-block object on the main list: pops a pool block, sets its handler a0 and links it before g_ObjListTail; the rest of the block is left as it was

name: Obj_FreeWithBlocks
purpose: returns object a6 and every nonzero block handle in its 8 words +8..+$17 to the pool free list (does not unlink it)

name: Obj_UnlinkFree
purpose: unlinks the one-block object a6 from its list and pushes the block back on the object pool

name: VIntObj_RunList
purpose: calls the handler of every object on the V-int object list with a6 = the object, until the tail sentinel's VIntObj_ListEnd returns for it

name: VIntObj_ListEnd
purpose: handler of the V-int list's tail sentinel: drops the jsr's return address so VIntObj_RunList returns to the V-int

name: VIntObj_InitList
purpose: empties the V-int object list: links g_VIntListHead straight to the tail sentinel g_VIntListTail and gives the sentinel the handler VIntObj_ListEnd

name: VIntObj_New
purpose: creates a one-block object on the V-int list: pops a pool block, sets its handler a0 and links it before g_VIntListTail, with g_VIntOff raised so a V-int during the link is skipped

name: VIntObj_NewIdle
purpose: VIntObj_New with the handler fixed to its own closing rts ($8BEC), so the object does nothing until the caller stores the real handler in (a6)

name: VIntObj_UnlinkFree
purpose: unlinks object a6 from the V-int list and returns its block to the object pool, with g_VIntOff raised so the V-int can't walk the list mid-edit

name: Hitbox_InitLists
purpose: empties both collision box lists: links g_PlayerBoxList to g_PlayerBoxTail and g_EnemyBoxList to g_EnemyBoxTail, each tail's next = 0

name: Hitbox_LinkPlayerList
purpose: appends collision box a0 to the end of g_PlayerBoxList (after g_PlayerBoxLast, before g_PlayerBoxTail)

name: Hitbox_LinkEnemyList
purpose: appends collision box a0 to the end of g_EnemyBoxList (after g_EnemyBoxLast, before g_EnemyBoxTail)

name: Hitbox_Unlink
purpose: unlinks collision box a0 from whichever box list it is on (prev.next = next, next.prev = prev)

name: Hitbox_FindPlayerBox
purpose: finds the first box on g_PlayerBoxList overlapping the rectangle d4-d6 x d5-d7

name: Hitbox_FindEnemyBox
purpose: finds the first box on g_EnemyBoxList overlapping the rectangle d4-d6 x d5-d7

name: Hitbox_FindNextBox
purpose: continues an overlap scan from the box after a2 (same rectangle test as Hitbox_FindPlayerBox)

name: Hitbox_FindPlayerBoxOfId
purpose: finds the first box on g_PlayerBoxList whose id (+$10) is d3 and that overlaps d4-d6 x d5-d7

name: Hitbox_FindNextBoxOfId
purpose: continues a Hitbox_FindPlayerBoxOfId scan from the box after a2

name: Obj_SpawnEnemy
purpose: spawns a 4-block script object (enemy, $58 = $A) at d4/d5 running script a2, linked on the main object list

name: Obj_SpawnEnemyOrQuit
purpose: spawns a 4-block enemy script object like Obj_SpawnEnemy, but returns to the caller's caller when the pool is short

name: Obj_SpawnEnemyNOrQuit
purpose: Obj_SpawnEnemyOrQuit with the block count in d7

name: Obj_SpawnEnemyAfter
purpose: Obj_SpawnEnemy with the object linked right after the running object (Obj_SpawnAfter): a 4-block script object (enemy, $58 = $A) at d4/d5 running script a2

name: Obj_SpawnBoss
purpose: spawns a 4-block script object with $58 = $B (boss class) at d4/d5 running script a2

name: Obj_SpawnBossOrQuit
purpose: spawns a 4-block $58 = $B script object, returning to the caller's caller when the pool is short

name: Obj_SpawnScriptedOrQuit
purpose: spawns a 4-block VM2_RunObject object at d4/d5, returning to the caller's caller when the pool is short

name: Obj_SpawnScripted
purpose: spawns a 4-block object run by VM2_RunObject at d4/d5, linked on the main object list

name: Obj_Spawn
purpose: allocates a d7-block object with handler a0, links it on the main object list and initialises it at d4/d5

name: Obj_SpawnScriptedUnlinked
purpose: spawns a 4-block VM2_RunObject object at d4/d5 without linking it on the main object list

name: Obj_SpawnUnlinked
purpose: allocates a d7-block object with handler a0 (not linked on the main object list) and initialises it at d4/d5

name: Obj_SpawnAfter
purpose: allocates a d7-block object with handler a0 linked right after the running object (Obj_NewMultiAfter) and initialises it at d4/d5 (Obj_InitSpawned)

name: Obj_InitSpawned
purpose: initialises a freshly allocated script object: clears its blocks, default hook scripts, position d4/d5, serial and sprite attribute

name: Hitbox_WipeEnemies
purpose: native callback: deals $200 damage to every enemy box and pauses spawning for 15 frames (screen clear)

name: Fx_SpawnAimedN
purpose: native callback: runs an a4 spawn script at a mirrored offset, heading = the object's heading rounded to one of N directions

name: Fx_SpawnAimed
purpose: native callback: runs an a4 spawn script at a mirrored offset with the object's own heading

name: Fx_SpawnAtOfs
purpose: native callback: runs an a4 spawn script at the object's x/y plus an offset mirrored by its flip bits, heading 0

name: Fx_SpawnKnockback
purpose: native callback: runs an a4 spawn script at a mirrored offset, the spawned objects inheriting 3/4 of the object's knockback speed

name: Fx_RunScriptArg
purpose: runs the a4 spawn script given by the script's next dc.l (Fx_RunScript)

name: Fx_RunScript
purpose: runs a4 spawn script a0 on g_SpawnCtx with the parent's velocity and flip, so the objects it spawns start from d2-d5

name: Fx_RunScriptNoParent
purpose: runs the a4 spawn script at a4 on g_SpawnCtx with the scene's default sprite attribute

name: Arc_HeadAtMark
purpose: a4 native: points the object's heading at the marked point (g_ArcTargetX/Y, set by Op2_FxMarkPlayerTarget): heading = Mot_Atan2 of the mark minus the object's x/y

name: Arc_PlanToArgs
purpose: a4 native: plans a gravity arc for the current a4 object to the target point given in the script

name: Wave_Start
purpose: spawns a wave-director object running a5 script a5 (handler $6A14) and counts it in g_WaveCount

name: Camera_IsLocked
purpose: native callback: d0 = 1 when g_CameraLockX holds a lock point, else 0 (for the switch op $2D40)

name: HUD_ShowGoSignCb
purpose: native callback: starts the GO! sign (HUD_StartGoSign) and returns d0 = 0

name: Camera_UpdateView
purpose: per frame: steps the screen shake and derives the view values from the camera (sprite offsets, on-screen and movement areas), and counts down two timers

name: Camera_TrackPlayersX
purpose: per frame: scrolls the camera right toward the players (their mean x when both play) or the lock point, then Camera_UpdateView

name: Pal_FlashWhite
purpose: native callback: flashes the screen white for 4 frames

name: Shake_StartIfIdle
purpose: native callback: starts the standard screen shake unless one is running

name: Shake_Start
purpose: starts the standard screen shake: 6 px up, pull 2 px per frame, and kicks the second oscillator

name: Shake_StartBig
purpose: starts the big screen shake: 12 px up, pull 3

name: Shake_Update
purpose: steps the screen-shake bounce and the second oscillator, and sets the view position (camera + shake)

name: Scroll_SetPlaneA
purpose: sets plane A's scroll words g_HScrollA / g_VScrollA from the map layer g_LayerA

name: Scroll_LayerToScroll
purpose: converts map layer a6's tile column/row and fine offsets into a plane H-scroll word (negated pixel x) and a V-scroll word (pixel y)

name: Scroll_RunParallax
purpose: selects the per-line scroll upload (g_ScrollMode $C) and runs a parallax command list that fills the line H-scroll buffers

name: Scroll_NextCmd
purpose: fetches the next parallax command word from a5 and dispatches it through the 4-byte jump table that follows (0 = end of list)

name: ScrollJt_LayerA
purpose: parallax command 4: jump-table slot that branches to ScrollCmd_LayerA

name: ScrollJt_CameraA
purpose: parallax command $C: jump-table slot that branches to ScrollCmd_CameraA

name: ScrollJt_CameraB
purpose: parallax command $14: jump-table slot that branches to ScrollCmd_CameraB

name: ScrollCmd_LayerA
purpose: parallax command 4: fills plane A's line H-scroll buffer in bands from a map layer's position and sets g_VScrollA to the layer's y

name: ScrollCmd_CameraA
purpose: parallax command $C: fills plane A's line H-scroll buffer in bands from the view position g_ViewX/g_ViewY and sets g_VScrollA

name: ScrollCmd_CameraB
purpose: parallax command $14: fills plane B's line H-scroll buffer in bands from the view position and sets the plane B V-scroll word

name: Scroll_BandsFromLayer
purpose: takes a map layer's pixel position as the band origin (x as 16.8, y) and falls into Scroll_FillBands

name: Scroll_FillBands
purpose: fills 224 screen lines of a line H-scroll buffer from a band table: bands above the view are skipped, each visible band's lines get -(x / divisor)

name: Rand_Next
purpose: steps the game's pseudo-random generator (shift/xor over a word and a long of state) and returns the new random word

name: Rand_Signed
purpose: returns a signed random number in [-d0/2, d0/2)

name: Rand_Below
purpose: returns an unsigned random number in [0, d0)

name: Mem_Clear
purpose: zeroes d7 bytes at a0, 32 bytes per loop, then words, then a last odd byte

name: Scene_InitStage
purpose: starts a gameplay section: common scene init, then reads the stage header for the movement area, two player-slot objects, both players' HUD and start positions, join offset, play mode, terrain routines and camera start, and fades in

name: Scene_InitPlain
purpose: starts a non-gameplay scene (title, menus, story, cards): common scene init from the a6 header, then starts the fade in

name: Scene_InitCommon
purpose: resets the machine for a new scene with the display off: clears work RAM, VRAM tables, CRAM and VSRAM, the object lists, pool, boxes and DMA queue, then applies the scene header (section id, art cache size, VDP registers, setup routine, DMA budget, sprite attribute, two mode flags)

name: Frame_BeginStage
purpose: starts a gameplay frame: marks the frame busy, resets the DMA queue and sprite list, the scene's fixed sprites ($F808), then the HUD and the shot-art keeper

name: Frame_Begin
purpose: starts a non-gameplay frame: marks it busy, resets the DMA queue and sprite list and adds the scene's fixed sprites ($F808), without the HUD

name: Frame_RunWorld
purpose: runs one gameplay step: the stage trigger table (Trigger_RunX), every object (Obj_RunList) and camera tracking (Camera_TrackPlayersX); with the debug free camera on it moves the camera instead

name: Frame_End
purpose: finishes a frame and waits for the vertical blank: builds the SAT, releases the frame to the V-int, resumes the background decompressor while waiting, then pause check, RNG step, the scene's per-frame callback and the frame counters

name: Pause_Update
purpose: in a stage, pauses when a player in play presses Start: holds the main loop until Start again, entering the debug pause menu when $F60E is set, else watching for the section-skip code B A Down B A Down Left Up C

name: SceneCb_None
purpose: the idle per-frame scene callback: returns at once (also the 'not yet' exit of the countdown callbacks)

name: Scene_FadeOutExit
purpose: starts the fade to black and installs SceneCb_WaitFadeExit, which leaves the scene loop once the fade is complete

name: Scene_EndAfterDelayWhite
purpose: a2 native: ends the scene after a delay with a fade to white and a result code

name: Player_GetP1Var1
purpose: if player 1 is in play, returns its object's script variable 1

name: Player_GetP2Var1
purpose: if player 2 is in play, returns its object's script variable 1

name: Main_Start
purpose: the game's main program after boot: clears RAM and VRAM/CRAM, starts the sound driver, seeds the RNG, sets the new-game defaults, then loops forever through attract, title, play, continue/game over and ending

name: Stage_Intro1
purpose: section $0001: stage 1's opening, stage music 8 then the scene list Tbl_00A166 ($4A180 shared stage opening, $4A216 stage 1)

name: Section_RunNext
purpose: looks up the section that follows g_SectionId in an order table, makes it current and calls its routine from Tbl_00A0AC

name: Scene_RunList
purpose: calls each scene routine of a zero-terminated long list in turn while g_SceneResult stays 0

name: Pad_CheckStart
purpose: a2 native test: reports whether Start was just pressed on pad 1 or 2 and records which pad

name: Sound_PlayMusic
purpose: switches the music to song d0 unless music is locked or that song is already playing

name: BgTask_Start
purpose: starts the LZ decompressor as the background task unless one is active: saves a context whose PC is the decompressor and whose registers carry its arguments

name: BgTask_Resume
purpose: if a background task is active, continues it where the V-int parked it: interrupts off, g_BgTaskRunning set, context restored, fake RTE to its PC/SR

name: Scene_ResetBufPtrs
purpose: points all 16 entries of the scene-script buffer pointer table $E092 at RAM $FF0000

name: Lz_Decompress
purpose: LZ77 decompressor (the background task's code): copies literals from a separate stream and matches from the output until the end code, then ends the background task

name: Pad_ReadAll
purpose: the V-int's full-path pad read: updates g_Pad1/g_Pad2 from ports 1 and 2 and copies both records to g_PadLive1/g_PadLive2

name: Pad_ReadLive
purpose: the V-int's busy-path pad read: updates g_PadLive1/g_PadLive2 directly from ports 1 and 2, so the pause code can poll the pads while the main loop is held

name: Pad_Update
purpose: reads one pad and updates its 4-byte record: held, previous, newly pressed, newly released

name: Pad_ReadPort
purpose: reads one 3-button pad port with the TH toggle and returns its buttons active-high, dropping opposite directions pressed together

name: Fade_Step
purpose: per-V-int palette fade: moves g_FadeLevel 2 toward g_FadeTarget every g_FadeDelay+1 frames, then rebuilds g_PalFaded from g_PalSource for each palette line whose brightness (level + line tint) changed or was reloaded

name: Pal_VIntUpload
purpose: V-int palette upload: runs the white flash (CRAM filled with $0EEE, restored when g_FlashTimer ends) or else DMAs the lines of g_PalFaded that Fade_Step rebuilt to CRAM

name: Fade_StartIn
purpose: starts a fade in: puts the palette fully faded (white when g_FadeLevel is already at +$E, else black) and sets target 0 at one step per 3 frames

name: Fade_ToNormal
purpose: fades the palette back to normal brightness from its current level, one step per 3 frames

name: Fade_StartOutBlack
purpose: starts the fade to black: target = -$E minus the largest line tint offset, so every channel of every line reaches black

name: Fade_StartOutWhite
purpose: starts the fade to white: target = +$E minus the smallest line tint offset, so every channel of every line reaches white

name: Fade_FlickerTarget
purpose: moves g_FadeTarget one step (2) up or down at random, kept within -2..+$C: a flickering brightness when called every frame

name: Fade_FlashWhite6
purpose: white flash: CRAM white for 2 frames, then the palette fades in from full white (+$E) one step per 6 frames

name: Fade_InFromPale6
purpose: jumps the palette to a pale level (+$A toward white) and fades it back to normal one step per 6 frames, without the CRAM white flash

name: Fade_MaxTint
purpose: returns the largest of the 12 per-line tint offsets (r/g/b of palette lines 0-3), at least -$E

name: Fade_MinTint
purpose: returns the smallest of the 12 per-line tint offsets (r/g/b of palette lines 0-3), at most +$E

name: Pal_LoadLine0
purpose: copies a 16-colour palette into line 0 of g_PalSource and flags the line for Fade_Step to rebuild

name: Pal_LoadLine1
purpose: copies a 16-colour palette into line 1 of g_PalSource and flags the line for Fade_Step to rebuild

name: Pal_LoadLine2
purpose: copies a 16-colour palette into line 2 of g_PalSource and flags the line for Fade_Step to rebuild

name: Pal_LoadLine3
purpose: copies a 16-colour palette into line 3 of g_PalSource and flags the line for Fade_Step to rebuild

name: Tint_FlashC1
purpose: starts a line-tint flash: g_TintLevel +$C decaying to 0 by 2 every frame

name: Tint_StepLine3
purpose: steps the line tint and applies it to palette line 3 (equal red, green and blue brightness offsets)

name: Tint_Step
purpose: moves g_TintLevel 2 toward g_TintTarget once every g_TintDelay+1 calls and returns it

name: VDP_ClearVRAM
purpose: zeroes all 64 KB of VRAM

name: VDP_ClearCRAM
purpose: sets all 64 CRAM colours to black

name: VDP_WhiteCRAM
purpose: sets all 64 CRAM colours to white ($0EEE)

name: VDP_ClearVSRAM
purpose: zeroes the 40 VSRAM words (all vertical scroll values)

name: VDP_ClearSAT
purpose: zeroes the sprite attribute table (VRAM $0000-$027F, 80 sprites)

name: VDP_ClearHScroll
purpose: zeroes VRAM $BC00-$C3FF: the H-scroll table (and the tile $5FC that VDP_ClearPlanes fills the planes with)

name: VDP_ClearPlanes
purpose: fills planes A and B (VRAM $C000-$FFFF) with tile $5FC, a blank tile

name: VDP_LoadRegs
purpose: writes VDP registers 0-18 from a table of 19 bytes

name: Scroll_SetMode
purpose: switches the V-int scroll upload to another mode with the V-int held off, turning H-ints off first

name: VInt_UploadScroll
purpose: the V-int's scroll upload: jumps through VInt_ScrollModeTbl by g_ScrollMode; every mode ends by turning the display back on (VDP reg 1 = $64)

name: VInt_ScrollModeTbl
purpose: jump table of the V-int scroll modes 0-$10 (bra.w per 4 bytes): 0 display on only, 4 jmp via the pointer $E55C, 8 H/V scroll longs, $C VSRAM + line-scroll DMA, $10 VSRAM + $AFDE

name: VInt_ScrollModeTbl28
purpose: jump table of the V-int scroll modes $28-$3C, which mostly end in the H-int raster setup ($B1E0)

name: VInt_BusyScroll
purpose: the busy-path V-int's scroll step: jumps through VInt_BusyScrollTbl by g_ScrollMode, whose entries turn the display back on, and for modes $28 and $34-$3C also re-arm the H-int raster (worker 13)

name: VInt_BusyScrollTbl
purpose: jump table of the busy-path scroll modes: entry 0 branches to the display-on routine $AF04 (entries 8-$10 follow in the next file)

name: VInt_BusyMode04
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $04: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyScrollTbl8
purpose: busy-path scroll jump table, modes 8-$10 (continues VInt_BusyScrollTbl): all three branch to VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a busy V-int uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyMode14
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $14: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyMode18
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $18: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyMode1C
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $1C: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyMode24
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $24: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyScrollTbl28
purpose: busy-path scroll jump table, modes $28-$2C: $28 re-arms the H-int raster (VInt_BusyRearmRaster), $2C only turns the display back on

name: VInt_BusyMode30
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $30: bra.w VInt_ScrollDisplayOn, so a dropped frame uploads no scroll

name: VInt_BusyScrollTbl34
purpose: busy-path scroll jump table, modes $34-$3C: re-arm the H-int raster (HInt_Rearm) so the per-line effect survives a dropped frame

name: VInt_BusyMode3C
purpose: busy-path V-int scroll slot for mode $3C: bra.w HInt_Rearm, as mode $38

name: VInt_ScrollDisplayOn
purpose: scroll mode 0 and the common tail of every mode: turns the display back on with DMA off (VDP reg 1 = $64)

name: VInt_ScrollLinesARaster
purpose: scroll mode $28: DMAs plane A's line H-scroll, then swaps and re-arms the H-int raster (per-line V-scroll)

name: VInt_BusyRearmRaster
purpose: busy-path entry for mode $28: re-arms the H-int raster on the table already shown (no swap)

name: Scroll_DMALinePairs
purpose: DMAs 448 words from $FFE1D2 (224 interleaved plane A/B line H-scroll pairs) to the H-scroll table at VRAM $BC00

name: Scroll_DMALines
purpose: DMAs both planes' per-line H-scroll: 224 words of g_HScrollLinesA to VRAM $BC00 and g_HScrollLinesB to $BC02, increment 4

name: Scroll_DMALinesA
purpose: DMAs plane A's per-line H-scroll only: 224 words of g_HScrollLinesA to VRAM $BC00, increment 4

name: Scroll_DMALinesB
purpose: DMAs plane B's per-line H-scroll only: 224 words of g_HScrollLinesB to VRAM $BC02, increment 4

name: Scroll_DMAColumns
purpose: DMAs 40 words of 2-cell column V-scroll (20 interleaved plane A/B pairs) from $FF9000 to VSRAM 0

name: Scroll_DMAColumnsAB
purpose: DMAs the column V-scroll of both planes from separate buffers: 20 words from $FF9000 to VSRAM 0 and 20 from $FF9028 to VSRAM 2, increment 4

name: HInt_InstallVScrollB
purpose: installs the per-line V-scroll raster for plane B: the H-int handler will write one word per line to VSRAM 2

name: Mem_FillRampRun
purpose: unrolled body of Mem_FillRamp: 224 8-byte units, each storing the integer word of the 16.16 accumulator d0 to (a0)+ and adding the step d1

name: Mem_FillWords
purpose: stores the word d0 d7 times at (a0)+ (up to 224: one per screen line)

name: Mem_FillWords2Run
purpose: unrolled body of Mem_FillWords2: units `move.w d0,(a0)+; move.w d2,(a1)+`, 128 from here to $CD7A (96 more identical units at $C9FA-$CB79 are never reached)

name: Span_ClearLinesRun
purpose: unrolled body of Span_ClearLines: 224 6-byte units `move.w d0,(a0)+; move.w d2,(a1)+; subq.w #1,d2`

name: Span_ClearLines
purpose: fills d7 lines of the span tables with 'no span': H-scroll d0 and a V-scroll that counts down one per line, so every line keeps showing the same plane row (row 0 when d2 = -line)

name: Span_FillRampsDither0Run
purpose: unrolled body of Span_FillRampsDither0: 18-byte units like Span_FillRamps' but the H-scroll word alternates and-$FFFE / or-1, so its bit 0 follows the line parity; 188 units here, 36 more identical ones at $D82C-$DAB3 are never reached

name: Span_FillRampsDither1Run
purpose: unrolled body of Span_FillRampsDither1: the twin of Span_FillRampsDither0Run with or/and swapped, so bit 0 runs 1, 0, 1 ...; 36 more units at $E81A-$EAA1 are never reached

name: Spr_MaskLeftColumn
purpose: when the scene asks for it (g_SceneFixedSpr), blanks the leftmost 16 screen pixels: queues a solid tile block once, then adds a column of 7 high-priority 16x32 sprites at screen x 0 to the SAT buffer every frame

name: Span_ClearScreen
purpose: clears the whole span picture: all 224 lines get H-scroll 0 and V-scroll -line (Span_ClearLines)

name: Span_DrawDiscDither
purpose: adds a dithered filled disc to the span tables, merging each line with a span already there (union of the two), from the half-width table g_CircleSpans

name: Span_ClearDrawDisc
purpose: clears all 224 span lines, then draws the dithered disc alone (Span_DrawDiscDither)

name: Span_BuildCircle
purpose: builds the half-width table of a circle of radius d0 for Span_DrawDiscDither: r+1 words at g_CircleSpans, from the top row (0) to the centre row (r), by the midpoint algorithm

name: Player_InitRecord
purpose: resets a player record for a new game or a join: score 0, health $100, charge 0, countdown 0, and the starting lives, weapon type and weapon level

name: Player_JoinOrSpawn
purpose: handler of a player slot object while no player is on screen: when the record is in play it spawns the player (3 pool blocks, Batman or Robin script, at the saved position or the camera + join offset with $78 frames of invulnerability) and switches to Player_Run; otherwise it waits for Start with a credit to join

name: Player_Despawn
purpose: takes a player out of play: handler back to Player_JoinOrSpawn, record in-play bit cleared, sprite frames and collision boxes released and the 3 pool blocks freed

name: Player_HurtFixed
purpose: a2 native: takes $20 (1/8 of full) health from the player without a hit; at 0 it plays sound request 1 and loses a life, and removes the player when none are left

name: Player_LoseLife
purpose: takes a life: with lives left, refills health, halves the weapon level and clears the countdown (d0 = 0); with none, zeroes lives and health and slides the HUD panel out (d0 = 1)

name: Player_SetExitFlag
purpose: for one player record in play: sets bit $800 of its script variable 1 (the player scripts walk off) and installs SceneCb_WaitPlayersExit

name: Player_SetBits300
purpose: sets bits $300 of one in-play player's script variable 1

name: Player_ClearBits300
purpose: clears bits $300 of one in-play player's script variable 1

name: EnemyAtk_HitTouch
purpose: enemy body-contact hit callback: when the target can be hit, adds the attacker's touch damage $12(a6) and a flinch (hit type 6), no spark

name: EnemyAtk_HitScriptSpark
purpose: a4 native hit: when the struck box can be hit, adds the script's damage word as a flinch (hit type 6) and puts the script's spark at the contact point; else skips both operands

name: EnemyAtk_DamageFoundBox
purpose: a2 native: damages the box found by the last overlap op (g_FoundBox) by the script word, as a flinch (hit type 6), if it can be hit

name: EnemyAtk_ApplyHit
purpose: common tail of EnemyAtk_HitPlayerA/B: damage +$34 to the box, knockback +$36 x 256 by the attacker's facing, hit type 7, a 7-frame movement pause for the attacker and the spark a1

name: Hitbox_CanHitTarget
purpose: hit test for enemy attacks: Hitbox_CanHitPlayer extended to owner id 5: accepts a struck box owned by id 5, 1 or 2 whose owner is not invulnerable and which was not struck yet

name: Hitbox_CanHitPlayer
purpose: hit test for attacks on players: accepts the struck box a2 when its owner id is 1 or 2 (a player), that player's invulnerability byte $16 of its a5 block is 0, and this box was not yet struck (sets box+$3C bit 0)

name: Hitbox_SpawnAtContact
purpose: spawns the a4 effect script a1 at the centre of the overlap between box a2 and the rectangle d4-d7 (via $91F2 on g_SpawnCtx), preserving the caller's registers

name: Hitbox_OverlapCenter
purpose: returns the centre of the intersection of box a2's rectangle (+$12..+$18) and the rectangle d4-d7

name: Weapon_KeepShotArt
purpose: keeps both players' current weapon-shot art resident in VRAM (Weapon_KeepShotArtOne for g_Player1 and g_Player2)

name: Weapon_KeepShotArtOne
purpose: for one player, loads the art of the shot frame for its weapon type/level (Tbl_010A1E, flying set when g_PlayMode bit 1) and releases the previously held frame 20 frames after a change, so shots spawn without an art load

name: Weapon_FireFlying
purpose: fires the player's weapon in the flying section: Weapon_Fire with the flying half ($C0) of Tbl_010AF8

name: Shot_DamageTarget
purpose: native hit op of the weapon-shot a4 scripts: marks the struck box hit, gives it the shot's knockback (+/-1.0 by the shot heading) and damage $12(a6), and branches the script on whether the box's energy ran out

name: Fx_SpawnSkidEffect
purpose: native op: while the mover touches terrain and brakes or reverses at speed, spawns the effect script Scr4_010D9A (or Scr4_010DAC moving left) every 4th frame at an operand offset with random x jitter

name: Coll_MoveScene
purpose: moves a box through the scene's terrain by calling g_TerrainFn, or g_TerrainFnAlt when the mover's flag bit 0 of (a3) is set

name: Coll_SetFlatFloor
purpose: makes the scene terrain a flat floor at height d0: installs Coll_FlatFloor / Coll_FlatFloorRest as the terrain routines

name: Player_NewGameSetup
purpose: starts a new game's player state: copies the boot settings $F610/$F612/$F61E/$F620 to $F634, g_Credits, $F64A, $F64C, then falls into Player_InitRecords

name: Player_InitRecords
purpose: resets both player records for a new game: picks which one is in play from g_StartPad, gives the Robin flag from g_P1IsRobin, sets pad numbers and default score/health/lives/weapon

name: HUD_Init
purpose: scene-start HUD reset: unlocks joining, queues the HUD art upload as the next HUD step and puts both player panels on their opening script

name: HUD_InitPanel
purpose: starts one player's HUD panel script: in play shows the stats, otherwise GAME OVER with PRESS START/credits or without credits

name: HUD_PlayerJoined
purpose: switches the HUD when the player a0 joins mid-game: its panel shows the credits, slides out and back with the stats; the other absent player's panel shows the zero-credit loop when no credits are left

name: HUD_PlayerOut
purpose: switches the HUD when player a0 has lost the last life: GAME OVER on both panels and joining locked when the other player is out too, otherwise GAME OVER then PRESS START/credits (or BOSS TIME while joining is locked)

name: HUD_ShowBossTime
purpose: puts one absent player's panel on the BOSS TIME / PLEASE WAIT / credits loop (Tbl_011012); players in play are left alone

name: HUD_ShowPressStart
purpose: puts one absent player's panel on the PRESS START / GAME OVER loop (Tbl_010FF6); players in play are left alone

name: Player_GatherStats
purpose: recomputes the per-frame aggregates over the players in play: count, and max/min/sum of weapon level, health/16 and lives

name: Player_AddStats
purpose: adds one player record to the per-frame aggregates when it is in play, otherwise clears its $36/$38/$3A fields

name: HUD_Update
purpose: per-frame HUD work: player aggregates, the two panels' scripts and slides, then the one DMA step selected by g_HUDStep

name: HUD_StepIdle
purpose: the HUD step jump table's offset-0 entry: no DMA this frame (the following nop pads the table to the HUD_StepBranches entries)

name: HUD_StepBranches
purpose: HUD step jump table entries 4-$14: one bra each to HUD_StepLoadArt, HUD_StepP1Ring, HUD_StepP1Panel, HUD_StepP2Ring, HUD_StepP2Panel

name: HUD_DrawWeaponBar
purpose: draws the weapon charge bar under the score into the panel buffer: fill from the charge byte +$8 (max $2B, flashing when full), colour set by weapon type +$28, alternate cells while the timer +$26 runs (blinking below 150)

name: HUD_DrawScore
purpose: draws the player's score (capped at 999999) as up to 6 digit tiles in the panel's top row, leading digits dropped and the rest padded by HUD_ClearTiles

name: HUD_DrawScoreDigit
purpose: emits one decimal digit of d0 for the place value d1 (repeated subtraction) and copies its tile into the HUD buffer

name: HUD_ClearTiles
purpose: clears d7 more tiles of the panel's top row (one per $60-byte column), padding after the score digits

name: HUD_DrawLifeRing
purpose: draws the 3x3-tile ring around the lives digit: segments from health +$4/16 (0-16), two animation tables alternated every 4 frames by counter +$24, then overlays the lives digit (+$6, max 9) on the centre tile

name: HUD_DrawPanelText
purpose: draws a 12-character panel message as 2 rows of 6 font tiles (ASCII - $20 through the glyph table)

name: HUD_RunPanelScript
purpose: steps one player's HUD panel script: counts down the wait timer +$1E and, when it reaches 0, runs ops from +$20 through the op table Tbl_011764 until one waits

name: HudOp_Halt
purpose: panel script op 0: stops the script on this op (timer 0, pointer kept)

name: HudOp_Wait
purpose: panel script op 4: waits the following word's number of frames

name: HudOp_Goto
purpose: panel script op 8: jumps by the following word, relative to the op, and keeps running

name: HudOp_SlideOut
purpose: panel script op $C: starts the panel sliding off its screen edge (calls $118E2) and keeps running

name: HudOp_SlideIn
purpose: panel script op $10: starts the panel sliding back in from its screen edge (calls $1189C) and keeps running

name: HudOp_WaitSlide
